description: Pivot WAKA from inspiration capture into an ambition mirror powered by a personal context graph. Keep the post-it Top of Mind metaphor, aggressively migrate naming, keep graph inspection internal, and add a first self-improving loop through user feedback.

Run API typecheck and targeted top-of-mind refresh tests

userStories.title: Make capture feel safe, autosaved, and highlightable
userStories.description: As a user, I want capture to feel like private note-taking in a safe zone, with autosaved drafts and an easy way to mark the parts that mattered most.

Autosave capture drafts locally and never clear text until server save succeeds
Add a way to highlight selected text as the part that hit most
Persist highlighted snippets or structured highlight metadata with the signal, or explicitly store them as signal metadata if a dedicated table is too large for this story

Show a brief post-capture confirmation that reflects what WAKA noticed without sounding final
Run web typecheck, targeted capture tests, and browser verification
userStories.notes: Capture should feel like a safe private scratchpad, not a high-pressure form. The user should not worry that a long personal note will disappear accidentally. Highlights are high-confidence resonance evidence for the context graph.

userStories.title: Create shareable Top of Mind value-prop page
userStories.description: As a user, I want a shareable Top of Mind page that explains what WAKA does while also showing my current provisional top-of-mind notes to other people.
acceptanceCriteria: Create or update the shareable Top of Mind page so it can explain the product and show the user’s current top-of-mind notes in one link

Replace placeholder narrative with stronger value-prop copy that explains: most inspiration disappears, WAKA catches what almost slipped away, and saved signals slowly form a picture of who the user wants to think with, where they want to be, and what they might be here to build
Make clear that the page is not manually written by the user; it is generated from things they saved and changes as new signals arrive
Clarify what the bottom post-it notes represent: provisional graph-backed reflections, tensions, questions, and action hints, not permanent identity claims
Keep the tone poetic but understandable enough that sharing the link explains why WAKA exists
Remove WOW terminology from this page entirely
Run web typecheck, targeted page/component tests, and browser verification
userStories.notes: Draft copy direction: Yun’s Top of Mind. Most inspiration disappears. This person caught it before it vanished. Slowly, the things they saved began to take shape: who they want to think with, where they want to be, what they might be here to build. They did not write all of this; they saved what almost slipped away, and the rest emerged. Not final. Changes as new signals arrive. This page was made from the things they saved. It changes every week. © WAKA, 2026, for minds that wander.

userStories.title: Add first decision memo scaffold for what to build
userStories.description: As a user, I want WAKA to turn my context graph into a lightweight decision memo for what to build next.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a backend or frontend scaffold for a what-to-build decision memo using existing context graph and top-of-mind evidence
Memo includes what the user seems drawn to, strongest evidence, tensions, and one testable next action
Keep this behind an internal or low-prominence route if the rest of the product is not ready
Add targeted tests for memo assembly with fixture graph data
Run relevant typechecks and tests

userStories.title: Create saved signal search and deep-dive experience
userStories.description: As a user, I want to search and deeply inspect the things I saved so the archive becomes a living context surface, not a flat list of old notes.
acceptanceCriteria: Create or upgrade a saved-signal archive surface with prominent search, filter, and sort controls for saved signals

Support deep-dive inspection of a saved signal with raw text, highlighted snippets, attachments or links, resonance feedback, signal packet interpretation, related context nodes, and related top-of-mind notes where available

Make search useful for both exact text and meaning-oriented exploration by surfacing matching snippets and related graph terms; if semantic search is too large for this story, design the UI/API boundaries so it can be added without replacing the surface
Add quick filters for signal type, high-resonance or highlighted signals, unresolved questions/tensions, and recently revisited items where data exists
Let users continue the loop from the deep dive by adding a reflection, marking what still matters, or correcting the interpretation
Avoid second-brain filing behavior: do not require manual folders or tags before the archive is useful
Remove WOW terminology from the archive and deep-dive experience entirely
Run API/web typechecks, targeted archive/search tests, and browser verification
userStories.notes: Brainstorm direction: search should answer both "where is that thing I saved?" and "what pattern was this part of?" The deep dive should show the raw saved note, the exact part that hit, WAKA's current interpretation, graph links, top-of-mind notes it influenced, and lightweight correction actions. Good modes: All signals, Highlighted, Tensions, Questions, People/places, Recently resurfaced. Results should show matching snippets, resonance markers, and why this result is relevant.

userStories.title: Remove WOW terminology from product-facing surfaces
userStories.description: As a developer, I need WOW terminology removed from product-facing UI, docs, prompts, API clients, and new domain services because WAKA is now an ambition mirror centered on top-of-mind notes and personal context.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit remaining user-facing inspiration, WOW, and meaning strings
Remove WOW terminology from visible UI copy, README/product docs, model prompts, API client names, and new top-of-mind/context services
Keep legacy database table or column names such as wow_moments and wow_score only when changing them would require a larger persistence migration
Any retained legacy WOW names must be isolated behind top-of-mind, resonance, or context adapters and documented as legacy compatibility only
Do not expose /api/wow-moments as the preferred product route; new user-facing code must use /api/top-of-mind
Run API and web typechecks plus the highest-value targeted regression tests
Update progress.txt Codebase Patterns with final naming conventions

userStories.title: Make capture a low-friction self-understanding moment
userStories.description: As a user, I want capture to feel valuable in the moment, not like required data entry for AI, by helping me quickly notice why a signal amused, moved, bothered, or pulled me before the feeling disappears.
acceptanceCriteria: Reframe capture as a micro self-understanding loop: save the signal, mark what hit, optionally name why it hit, and receive a lightweight reflection without waiting for a later Top of Mind surface
Add low-friction emotion, resonance, or stakes controls using compact emoji/icon chips or similarly lightweight interactions rather than long forms
Support ambition-relevant reasons for saving such as amused me, I want this, I admire this, I envy this, feels like me, bothers me, makes me curious, high-stakes, and not sure
Let users skip every explicit input beyond the raw save without guilt, blocking, or degraded confirmation
Make the interaction feel fun and safe, not like tagging, journaling homework, a mood tracker, or engagement bait
Use progressive disclosure: show one simple prompt first, then offer an optional deeper question such as why did this amuse me or what part do I want more of
Persist emotion/reason/stakes metadata with the signal using the existing safest persistence path or a dedicated structure if already available
Use human-provided capture metadata in post-capture confirmation and make it available to signal packet/context graph interpretation as stronger evidence than model inference alone
Keep capture friction minimal on mobile and desktop, including keyboard-only and touch-friendly paths
Remove any WOW terminology from this capture flow
Run web typecheck, targeted capture tests, and browser verification
userStories.notes: Product rationale: in a world where AI can sense passively, asking humans for explicit input must be worth it immediately. The human-only value is not just emotion labeling; it is the user noticing why this signal mattered while the feeling is still alive. Capture should become a tiny revelation loop: this amused me, this made me envious, this feels like a life I want, this bothers me, this is high-stakes. Good interaction directions: one-tap chips, quick highlight plus reason, optional micro-question, press-and-hold intensity, or a tiny palette after selection. The goal is to reduce churn by making explicit input feel rewarding, clarifying, and uniquely human, not like feeding the AI.

userStories.title: Rebuild Top of Mind as ambition mirror statements
userStories.description: As a user, I want Top of Mind post-its to help me discover my ambition and internal frequency, not summarize the things I saved or label context graph nodes.
acceptanceCriteria: Change the Top of Mind generation architecture so every active note is grounded in an ambition dimension such as place, people, work, taste, tension, identity, rejection, or next experiment
Generate post-it titles as ambient-signal mirror statements about desired environments, desired peer groups, work direction, operating standards, rejected contexts, or emerging self-image
Do not use raw context node labels, saved-signal summaries, tags, or generic phrases such as "You keep circling X" as the main post-it text
Each Top of Mind note must expose why this may matter for ambition and 2-5 supporting saved signals or explicit evidence previews where available
Add deterministic tests that fail if a generated Top of Mind title is only a graph label, a saved content summary, or a shallow theme label
Update Home and share-page copy/rendering only as needed so the visible post-its read like ambition mirror statements on first load, not archive summaries
Ensure user feedback remains connected to the note and can validate or correct the ambition dimension, not just the underlying graph node
Run API and web typechecks, targeted Top of Mind generation tests, targeted Home/share tests, and browser verification of the exact Home Top of Mind path
userStories.notes: Product rationale: Paul Graham's cities essay points at ambient ambition signals: some rooms say you should be richer, smarter, braver, more tasteful, faster, freer, or more original. WAKA should help users infer which ambient signals they are already responding to. A useful post-it should read like: "You seem pulled toward places where ambitious people make things in public," "You may be trying to leave environments that reward consensus over aliveness," or "You seem to want peers who act before permission arrives." It should not read like: "founder cities," "rituals keep returning," or "You keep circling founder cities."

userStories.title: Update internal context dashboard for ambition graph debugging
userStories.description: As an internal operator, I need the context dashboard to make ambition graph quality readable and navigable, including restoring individual node dragging.
acceptanceCriteria: Keep the context dashboard internal/admin-only and do not turn the graph inspector into the primary user-facing product UI
Show ambition dimension or derived ambition role for context nodes where available, including place, people, work, taste, tension, identity, rejection, and next experiment
Add practical filters/search for node type, ambition dimension, confidence/weight, active versus stale status, and text labels
Improve the selected-node detail panel so it clearly shows supporting saved signals, related Top of Mind notes, related feedback, and why the node may matter for ambition
Restore individual node dragging in the graph; dragging one node must not move the entire connected component unless a group-drag mode is explicitly selected
Make the dashboard readable on common desktop widths without dense overlapping text or hard-to-scan panels
Add targeted tests or browser verification that selecting/filtering nodes works and that individual node drag behavior is restored
Run web typecheck and any targeted context-dashboard tests
userStories.notes: This is internal tooling for judging whether WAKA is learning ambition. The dashboard should help debug how saved signals become context nodes, ambition dimensions, Top of Mind notes, and feedback-adjusted confidence. Current pain points: hard to read/navigate, and graph nodes that used to be individually draggable now appear to drag only as connected groups.

userStories.title: Rebuild All Signals as an in-place inspiration revisit experience
userStories.description: As a user, I want the All Signals tab to feel like gently revisiting what I once loved inside the Top of Mind experience, not navigating to a complicated archive page.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking the Home All Signals tab must stay within the Top of Mind shell instead of navigating to a completely separate page
Replace the dense archive/search-page feel with an in-place surface whose visual language matches the Top of Mind post-it world
Make deep diving past inspirations feel calm, personal, and therapeutic: revisiting what once hit, what still feels alive, what changed, and what it may reveal about ambition
Reduce navigation complexity by using a simple browse-and-revisit flow before advanced search/filter controls; advanced controls should be secondary or progressively disclosed
Avoid the current narrow-sidebar deep dive pattern and avoid an admin-dashboard feel
Show the raw saved inspiration prominently, with highlighted parts, original context, gentle reflection prompts, related Top of Mind notes, and one lightweight way to mark whether it still matters
Keep any full `/signals` route only as an optional compatibility/deep link if needed; the primary product path from Home must be in-place
Add targeted Home/All Signals tests proving the tab does not route away and that the revisit/deep-dive surface renders in the Home experience
Run web typecheck, targeted tests, and browser verification for the exact Home All Signals path on desktop and mobile
userStories.notes: Product correction: the current `/signals` archive is too complicated and feels like a search/admin surface. The user wants past inspirations to feel like therapy: a soft return to what they once loved, with enough structure to notice whether the signal still matters and how it connects to ambition. All Signals should share the Top of Mind look and feel, stay in the same product world, and make deep dive emotionally legible before it becomes searchable.

userStories.title: Generate internal-frequency ambient signals for Top of Mind
userStories.description: As a user, I want Top of Mind to help me identify the ambient signals I am trying to live near, so I can understand which cities, rooms, peers, and environments match my ambition.
acceptanceCriteria: Add an explicit internal-frequency or ambient-signal layer above individual context nodes; Top of Mind must infer what kind of surrounding signal the user seems to be seeking, not only rephrase one graph node

Each primary Top of Mind post-it must answer one of these questions: what kind of city/room would make me more alive, what kind of people should I think with, what standard should feel normal around me, what environment am I rejecting, or what version of myself am I trying to become

Generate user-facing copy in the form of ambient signals such as "You may be looking for places that quietly tell you to be braver" or "You seem to want peers who make fast, public building feel normal"
Avoid generic ambition wrappers and label interpolation patterns such as "rooms where X can become normal", "work that turns X visible", or any sentence that still reads like a graph-label summary
Use multiple saved signals or multiple context nodes where possible so a Top of Mind note reflects a frequency pattern rather than a single extracted theme
Expose the ambient signal, matched environment, anti-environment, and evidence rationale in the Top of Mind API or note surface without leaking admin graph internals
Update Home and share-page rendering so the first-read value is the internal-frequency insight, with evidence available second
Add deterministic tests that fail when a generated note can be reduced to a single context label or does not mention an ambient signal, environment, peer group, standard, rejection, or self-image
Run API and web typechecks, targeted Top of Mind generation/API tests, targeted Home/share tests, and browser verification of the exact Home Top of Mind path
userStories.notes: Product correction after US-018: ambition dimensions and mirror-style templates are not enough. Paul Graham's cities frame is about ambient external signals: a city tells you to be richer, smarter, more ambitious, more tasteful, freer, braver, or more original. WAKA should infer the user's internal frequency so they can match it to cities, rooms, peers, and work environments. The post-it should not merely say what the saved things are about; it should say what kind of surrounding signal the user seems to need.

userStories.title: Make Top of Mind read like first-person jotting
userStories.description: As a user, I want generated Top of Mind post-its to sound like provisional notes I might have jotted to myself, not like an external AI describing me.
acceptanceCriteria: Change primary Top of Mind titles and first-read Home/share copy to first-person note-to-self language with direct, credible phrasing such as "I need rooms where...", "I want people who...", or "I am done with environments that..."
Avoid second-person or third-person framing in the main post-it text, including "you seem", "you may", "this person", and "WAKA thinks" unless it appears in secondary explanatory copy
Keep the tone scratchpad-like and replaceable without using weak hedges such as "I think", "maybe", "might", "probably", "seems", or "kind of" in primary post-it text
Preserve the internal-frequency / ambient-signal goal from US-021: first-person notes must still point at cities, rooms, peers, standards, anti-environments, or emerging self-image
Keep evidence and provenance available as secondary support so the product remains generated from saved signals rather than pretending the user literally typed the note
Update Top of Mind generation, legacy note serialization, Home rendering, share-page rendering, and tests as needed so existing/generated notes use the first-person voice

Add deterministic tests that fail if primary Top of Mind titles begin with or prominently use "You", "Your", "This person", "WAKA", raw graph labels, or weak hedges such as "I think", "maybe", "might", "probably", or "seems"
Run API and web typechecks, targeted Top of Mind generation/API tests, targeted Home/share tests, and browser verification of the exact Home Top of Mind path
userStories.notes: Product correction after US-021: even good ambient-signal notes can feel wrong if WAKA speaks about the user from the outside. The post-it metaphor works better if the text feels like the user's own direct jotting: "I need a city that makes brave work feel normal" or "I want peers who make building in public less weird." Keep the page honest that WAKA generated the notes from saved signals, but make the post-it itself feel first-person, credible, and replaceable without hedging language.

userStories.title: Reset product architecture around reflective ambition mirror
userStories.description: As a user, I want WAKA to feel like a private reflective room for understanding what I am becoming, not a productivity dashboard or second-brain archive.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit the current primary user-facing flows and identify/remove or demote surfaces that feel like productivity dashboards, archive management, generic AI insights, graph UI, or separate app sections that break the reflective world
Define the core product spaces in code and copy as Capture, Five Top of Mind post-its, Signal Revisit/Memory Drawer, Share, and Internal Debug
Keep the five post-it Top of Mind metaphor as the primary home object because post-its are ephemeral, replaceable, human, and aligned with personal context as the moat while software is ephemeral
Preserve existing useful data and APIs where practical, but allow aggressive UI, naming, route, and component restructuring if it improves the end-to-end reflective experience
Ensure product-facing copy frames WAKA as preserving what moved the user and reflecting what it may mean, not remembering everything or organizing knowledge
Keep admin/graph/debug concepts internal and out of the primary user experience
Document the new experience architecture in progress.txt so later loops do not regress into dashboard/archive/productivity patterns
Run web typecheck and targeted smoke tests for the Home route
userStories.notes: Product reset: WAKA should feel like a private place where what moved the user becomes a living map of who they are becoming. The hierarchy should be blank-page capture for what I feel now, five post-its for what keeps mattering, memory drawer for what I saved, and internal graph only as invisible machinery.

userStories.title: Rebuild capture as private reflection ritual
userStories.description: As a user coming out of a high-emotion, high-stakes, or ambiguous moment, I want capture to feel safe, quick, and immediately self-revealing instead of like manual data entry for AI.
acceptanceCriteria: Redesign the capture entry experience around a blank-page/private-weather feeling with the primary prompt "What almost slipped away?"
Keep capture one click away from the main experience and avoid adding a top-level capture tab or heavy form flow
Support messy text, links, images/files where already supported, and add or preserve a low-friction path for quickly saving before reflection
Make autosave/private safety visible near the writing area and never clear unsaved content until persistence succeeds
Keep highlighting "what hit" as a first-class action for long pasted text or quotes

Replace or refine resonance chips into emotionally precise human pulls such as I want this, I miss this, I envy this, this hurt, this scared me, this feels like me, this is not me anymore, I want people like this, I want to build toward this, I want to live near this, and I don't know yet
After save, show a tiny non-final mirror that gives immediate value, with actions to keep, adjust, or just save without interpretation
Ensure capture metadata and user-written micro-reflections persist as privileged evidence for downstream signal packets and ambition synthesis
Run targeted capture tests, web typecheck, and browser verification on desktop and mobile capture
userStories.notes: The friction of explicit human input should become the product's value. AI can summarize what happened; WAKA should preserve what it meant to the user. Capture should feel like a quiet ritual, not a form.

userStories.title: Make five ephemeral Top of Mind post-its the core surface
userStories.description: As a user, I want exactly five replaceable Top of Mind post-its that show the current shape of my ambition, not summaries of saved content.
acceptanceCriteria: Home should center exactly five Top of Mind post-it slots when enough context exists; low-data states should still point users into capture without becoming a dashboard
Each post-it must be first-person, direct, credible, and scratchpad-like without weak hedges or external diagnosis
Each post-it must represent a memory movement or ambition direction, not a topic summary, graph label, or saved-content summary
Add visible memory-state labels such as keeps returning, newly forming, came back, fading, tension, or needs testing
Post-it details should make replaceability explicit through copy such as not final, changed by new signals, replaced, or still here
Include light evidence affordances without making the first-read surface feel analytical or admin-like
Feedback should allow true, partly, not this, and rewrite in my words so the user shapes the post-it rather than merely rating AI
Update Home and share rendering, API surfaces if needed, and tests so regressions to summary-like Top of Mind fail
Run API/web typechecks, targeted Top of Mind tests, and browser verification of the Home path
userStories.notes: Five post-its are the main product object. They should feel temporary, important, movable, and replaceable: the current five things sitting on the front of the user's mind.

userStories.title: Add memory movement model for personal context
userStories.description: As a user, I want WAKA to evolve like memory by reinforcing, forgetting, reactivating, and surfacing contradictions as new signals arrive.
acceptanceCriteria: Introduce a persisted or derivable memory-state layer for context patterns with states including emerging, active, fading, dormant, reactivated, contradicted, and needs_testing
Track or derive first_seen_at, last_seen_at, reinforcement_count, recent_reinforcement_count, current_weight, confidence, decay, and supporting signal ids for memory patterns

New signals should be evaluated as reinforcing an existing pattern, creating a new emerging pattern, reactivating an old pattern, contradicting an active pattern, or contributing to decay by omission over time
Decay should reduce dominance of old unrepeated patterns without deleting historical context
Reactivation should make an old pattern meaningful again when new evidence returns after dormancy
Contradictions should be preserved as live tensions rather than averaged into bland balanced statements
Top of Mind selection should prioritize meaningful memory movement, not only highest-weight graph nodes
Add deterministic tests for reinforcement, decay, reactivation, contradiction, and Top of Mind selection from memory movement
Run API typecheck and targeted memory-model tests
userStories.notes: This is the core self-evolving loop. Personal context should behave more like memory than a static graph: what returns matters more, what stops returning fades, what comes back after dormancy becomes meaningful, and contradictions reveal live ambition tensions.

userStories.title: Build bounded ambition synthesis loop
userStories.description: As a user, I want WAKA to synthesize ambition only when there is enough evidence, so insights feel specific and earned rather than token-heavy generic AI output.
acceptanceCriteria: Create an event-triggered ambition synthesis path that runs only for qualified clusters, memory movements, explicit deep dives, weekly refreshes, strong user feedback, corrections, or contradictions
Keep cheap deterministic graph/memory updates continuous and reserve model-heavy divergent synthesis for bounded evidence sets

Synthesis input must include selected saved signals, highlights, emotional pull metadata, user micro-reflections, prior feedback, rewrites, memory state, and rejected/competing interpretations where available

Synthesis output must include a first-person post-it candidate, memory state, what environment it points toward, what it rejects, evidence rationale, confidence, and a rejected alternative interpretation
User correction and rewrite should update future synthesis behavior and not just the visible text
Prevent generic outputs by testing against shallow categories such as startups, comedy, cities, AI, inspiration, or productivity unless the output states the user's personal edge
Add token-budget safeguards, bounded input limits, idempotency, and fallback deterministic generation when synthesis is unavailable
Run API typecheck and targeted synthesis tests with mocked model/provider behavior
userStories.notes: Do not build an always-on token furnace. Build Ambition Synthesis as a gated, evidence-bounded loop that produces what deterministic ranking cannot: the personal edge connecting what moved the user.

userStories.title: Rebuild post-it deep dive as peel-open reflection
userStories.description: As a user, I want opening a Top of Mind post-it to feel like peeling it open into a calm reflective space, not inspecting a narrow sidebar or admin panel.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace any narrow-sidebar post-it detail pattern with a full-screen or large focused reflection surface that visually grows from the selected post-it
The opened post-it should preserve the first-person note as the emotional anchor
Show what this note points toward, what it rejects, what changed recently, memory state, and why it is currently on top of mind
Show 2-5 supporting saved moments with highlights and enough original context to feel emotionally grounded
Show rejected alternative interpretation where available so the user can see why WAKA chose this read instead of a shallow one
Provide true, partly, not this, and rewrite in my words controls, with rewrite treated as a first-class learning signal
Keep the visual language paper/post-it based and avoid cards-inside-cards, dense tables, or graph/admin terminology
Add targeted Home deep-dive tests and browser verification on desktop and mobile
userStories.notes: Deep diving should feel like reflective self-understanding. The user is not opening a database record; they are opening the current note their saved life has written back to them.

userStories.title: Rebuild saved signals as memory drawer
userStories.description: As a user, I want revisiting saved signals to feel like returning to moments that once moved me, not searching an archive.
acceptanceCriteria: Rename or reframe All Signals toward a softer memory-drawer concept while preserving compatibility routes if needed
Organize the primary revisit experience by emotional/memory sections such as still alive, changed shape, forgotten but returning, from an older version of me, keeps coming back, and tensions
Search and filters should be available but secondary or progressively disclosed, not the main posture of the page
Opening a saved signal should use a calm full-width reflective surface rather than a narrow sidebar

The signal detail should show original content, highlighted part, emotional pull at capture time, what it may mean now, related Top of Mind post-its, and prompts like what did this mean then, what does it mean now, and is this still me
Provide still alive, changed shape, not anymore, and optional what changed feedback, feeding the memory movement model
Keep the visual language consistent with the Top of Mind post-it world and avoid archive/admin/dashboard styling
Add targeted tests for in-place navigation, memory sections, signal detail, and feedback persistence
Run web typecheck and browser verification on desktop and mobile
userStories.notes: Saved signals are not files. They are the drawer beneath the desk: the moments, quotes, images, and fragments the five post-its emerged from.

userStories.title: Rebuild share page around living Top of Mind value prop
userStories.description: As a user, I want to share one link that both explains WAKA and shows my current living Top of Mind without feeling like a marketing page.
acceptanceCriteria: Share page should foreground the user's five current post-its and explain that they emerged from saved signals, corrections, returns, and things that changed shape

Copy should clearly communicate the value prop: most inspiration disappears; WAKA catches what moved the user and turns it into a changing map of what they may want to build, who they want around them, and where they may need to be
Avoid claiming the user literally wrote generated post-its; provenance should be honest but poetic
Use the post-it metaphor and ephemeral/change language prominently: not final, changes with new signals, personal context is alive
Do not create a separate generic landing page; the share page itself should explain the product through the user's current Top of Mind
Make privacy boundaries clear and do not expose raw saved signals unless an explicit sharing model exists
Update tests for share rendering and no raw private signal leakage
Run web typecheck and browser verification of the share page
userStories.notes: The share page should sell the product by showing the user's living Top of Mind. It should feel like: these post-its were not directly written by the user; they came from what the user saved, corrected, returned to, and outgrew.

userStories.title: Update internal debug for memory and synthesis quality
userStories.description: As an internal operator, I need to debug whether WAKA is truly learning ambition through memory movement and synthesis rather than producing nice-sounding summaries.
acceptanceCriteria: Keep this dashboard internal/admin-only
Show memory states, reinforcement, decay, reactivation, contradiction, feedback, rewrites, and supporting signals for each active pattern
For each Top of Mind post-it, show why it exists now, what changed recently, what evidence supports it, what alternative interpretation was rejected, and what feedback has shaped it
Add quality indicators that help detect shallow summaries, raw graph labels, generic ambition wrappers, and unsupported synthesis
Allow filtering by memory state, ambition dimension, confidence, stale/fading status, contradicted status, and recent user correction
Preserve or restore graph navigation only as internal diagnostic context; do not make graph inspection part of the user-facing experience
Add targeted internal-dashboard tests or browser verification
Run web/API typechecks and targeted admin tests
userStories.notes: Internal debug should serve product truth: is WAKA learning what actually moves the user, or just generating aesthetic summaries? This should help inspect the memory loop and ambition synthesis loop without leaking machinery into the user experience.

userStories.title: Generate Top of Mind in post-it thought language
userStories.description: As a user, I want Top of Mind post-its to sound like compressed private thoughts I might quickly jot down, not forced first-person AI insight sentences.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace the primary Top of Mind voice rule from forced first-person sentence starts to post-it thought language: fragments, questions, imperatives, tensions, and shorthand are allowed
Primary post-it text should usually be concise, preferably 3-9 words and no more than 12 words unless the evidence genuinely requires it
Avoid forced starts such as "I need", "I want", and "I am done with" in generated primary post-it text unless they sound natural and are not template-like
Continue banning outside diagnostic voice such as "you seem", "you may", "this person", "WAKA thinks", and generic AI framing
Generated post-its must still point at ambition context such as people, place, work, taste, rejection, identity, tension, or next experiment

Replace deterministic fallback templates with natural sticky-note phrasing such as "people who make courage normal", "public before perfect", "consensus rooms make me go quiet", "sharper taste as the default", or "test it in public"
Remove visible top metadata from post-it cards such as "no. 01", "keeps returning", or other status labels; keep any memory movement metadata inside the opened detail view or internal debug only
Do not render empty or weak Top of Mind slots at all; show only meaningful post-its that have earned the surface
Update generation, serialization/normalization, Home rendering, tests, and internal quality checks so summary-like, overly polished, or template-like post-it text fails
Run API/web typechecks, targeted Top of Mind generation tests, targeted Home tests, and browser verification of the Home Top of Mind path
userStories.notes: Product correction: first-person notes like "I need rooms where..." and "I want peers who..." sound unnatural when forced. Top of Mind should read like a sticky note from the user's inner weather: "people who make courage normal", "not another impressive path", "softness without losing intensity", "what does this envy know?", "make the thing before explaining it". The post-it should feel compressed, specific, replaceable, and ambition-relevant without sounding like a generated affirmation.

userStories.title: Add Memory Drawer relationship constellation
userStories.description: As a user, I want the Memory Drawer to show how saved inspirations are secretly talking to each other, with distinct visual forms for notes, links, images, and other signal types.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a Memory Drawer constellation mode or section that visually connects related saved signals instead of presenting only a linear list/search experience

Represent different saved signal input types with distinct paper-like visual treatments: typed notes as small handwritten scraps, links as quote/link cards with source/hostname, images as photo-like tiles, mixed/file signals as layered scraps
Use existing signal kind, attachments, highlighted snippets, and saved-signal detail data to decide each visual treatment; do not make every inspiration look like the same card
Draw soft relationship lines or arrows between related signals using existing meaning edges, related context terms, related Top of Mind notes, or bounded relationship synthesis where available

Relationship labels must use post-it thought language, not graph/admin language; examples include "same room, different mask", "this came back later", "the envy points here", "old self arguing with new self", or "both want the same people"
Clicking a relationship should open a calm explanation of why those memories are connected, including the two or more source inspirations, highlighted parts, and the relationship label
Allow lightweight user feedback on a relationship: true, not connected, better label; corrections should feed relationship quality or future synthesis where possible

Keep the constellation emotionally readable and sparse on desktop and mobile; avoid dense network graph aesthetics, node jargon, force-directed admin visuals, overlapping text, or tiny unreadable labels
Keep search/list as secondary support inside Memory Drawer, not the primary emotional posture
Add targeted web tests proving typed note, link, image, and mixed signal visuals render differently, relationship labels render without graph terminology, and relationship feedback can be submitted
Run web typecheck, targeted Home/Memory Drawer tests, and browser verification of the Memory Drawer constellation on desktop and mobile
userStories.notes: Product direction: Memory Drawer should become a constellation of saved moments, like a quote card connected by a soft arrow to a post-it that names the relationship. This is not an admin graph. It should feel like the user's saved notes, links, images, and screenshots are starting to speak to each other. Different input types should look materially different so a typed thought, a link, and an image are emotionally legible at a glance.

userStories.title: Make post-it thought language interpretable
userStories.description: As a user, I want Top of Mind post-its to stay natural and quick-jotted without becoming overly short slogans that no longer explain my ambition.
acceptanceCriteria: Update Top of Mind generation and fallback rules so post-it thought language is compressed but interpretable, not short at all costs
Primary post-it text should usually be 6-14 words; allow shorter only when the phrase is still concretely meaningful
Avoid ultra-short slogan outputs such as "public before perfect", "taste as default", "test it outside", or "courage normal" when they do not carry enough personal meaning
Each post-it should include or imply a concrete ambition object such as people, room, city, work, path, taste, life, self, standard, or experiment
Each post-it should imply a reason, contrast, or tension, not only a vibe or abstract value
Keep the post-it voice natural: fragments, imperatives, questions, and tensions are allowed, but avoid forced starts like "I want", "I need", and "I am done with" unless genuinely natural
Keep banning outside diagnostic voice such as "you seem", "you may", "this person", "WAKA thinks", and generic AI summary language

Replace deterministic examples with more interpretable phrases such as "make the thing before explaining it", "people who make courage feel normal", "a room where unfinished ambition is allowed", "stop mistaking safety for clarity", "not another impressive path that feels dead", or "find people who make building feel less lonely"
Update tests so slogan-like, too-short, or vague post-its fail while natural 6-14 word private notes pass
Run API/web typechecks, targeted Top of Mind generation tests, targeted Home tests, and browser verification of the Home Top of Mind path
userStories.notes: Product correction after US-032: the app overcorrected from forced first-person sentences into phrases that can be too short to be useful. The target is not slogans. A good post-it should be short enough to feel quickly jotted, but complete enough to help the user recognize themself.

userStories.title: Rebuild Memory Drawer with canvas and chronological card modes
userStories.description: As a user, I want the Memory Drawer to let me either revisit saved inspirations as a simple chronological card stack or explore how those inspirations connect on a low-fidelity relationship canvas.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace the current Memory Drawer layout with two clear modes: a chronological card mode and a relationship canvas mode
Provide an obvious, lightweight mode switcher for List and Graph/Canvas without navigating away from the Top of Mind experience
List mode should show saved inspirations as clean bounded cards ordered by when they were added, newest first by default
List mode should preserve the same card visual language as canvas mode, but arranged in a calm readable stream for scanning what was saved over time
Canvas mode should show a board experience where each saved inspiration is its own bounded card
Every inspiration card must have a max visual size and truncate long text after a few lines, with a clear way to open the full memory without expanding the entire board
Cards should feel lower-fidelity than Top of Mind post-its: small scraps, clipped notes, quote cards, link slips, image tiles, or layered paper depending on the saved signal type
Differentiate user-typed notes, links, images, mixed/file saves, and highlighted excerpts using existing saved signal fields and attachments where available
In Canvas mode, show relationships directly with soft arrows, lines, or nearby connector labels between inspiration cards; the board should make the user see why saved moments belong near each other
Relationship labels must be sparse, human, and optional; avoid graph terms, model terms, confidence scores, node jargon, cluster names, and category headings
Remove memory movement as a user-facing categorization method from the Memory Drawer, including labels, filters, sections, or explanatory copy
Remove dense sidebars, narrow detail panes, multi-column admin panels, and search-first navigation from both Memory Drawer modes
Search may remain as a small supporting control in either mode, but it must not become the primary structure of the experience
Opening a card should show only the full saved inspiration, its user note/highlights if present, and the few relationship explanations needed to understand why it is connected
The canvas should remain emotionally readable on desktop and mobile: no overlapping text, no tiny nodes, no force-directed graph behavior, and no unreadable relationship tangles

Add targeted Home/Memory Drawer tests proving List and Canvas modes switch correctly, chronological ordering is respected, cards are bounded/truncated, signal types render differently, relationship connectors render, and memory movement copy does not render
Run web typecheck, targeted Home/Memory Drawer tests, and browser verification of both Memory Drawer modes on desktop and mobile
userStories.notes: Product correction after seeing the Memory Drawer result: the current version gives the user too much to parse and too little to feel. The target has two modes. List mode is the clean chronological way to revisit what was saved in the order it entered WAKA. Canvas mode is the lower-fidelity evidence board where small bounded inspiration cards connect to each other. Top of Mind is polished post-its for current ambition; Memory Drawer is the evidence underneath. No memory movement taxonomy should be visible here.

userStories.title: Generate meaningful action checklist post-it from Top of Mind evidence
userStories.description: As a user, I want WAKA to turn my current Top of Mind into a small draggable action post-it with concrete real-world experiments that actually help me learn about my ambition.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace the current shallow actionForThoughtCard title/dimension template fallback with a grounded action generation layer that uses Top of Mind note evidence, saved signal previews, highlights, ambient signal, matched environment, anti-environment, evidence rationale, and ambition dimension

Generated actions must be concrete, small, and real-world rather than reflective homework; valid actions include messaging a specific kind of person, visiting or testing a type of room/city/environment, making or sharing a rough artifact, removing one environmental pull, or running a career/build experiment

Reject generic actions such as "do one tiny test", "explore this more", "reflect on this", "journal about this", "learn more", "think about", "research", or actions that simply repeat the post-it title
Each action must be visibly connected to one Top of Mind post-it or its supporting evidence, but the action text should stand alone and feel useful without exposing admin graph language
Action text should be specific enough that the user can do it within 24-72 hours; avoid broad life advice, vague self-improvement language, and corporate productivity phrasing
Show at most five active actions globally on the Top of Mind page; do not render weak, empty, duplicate, or low-confidence action slots
Make the action checklist its own draggable paper object on the Top of Mind wall, using the same drag behavior as the Top of Mind post-its
Users must be able to mark an action done or remove it from the active list; completed and removed actions should disappear from the visible active checklist
Add deterministic API/unit or web tests that fail when action generation returns generic/template actions or actions disconnected from evidence
Add Home tests proving the action checklist renders only meaningful actions, supports done/remove, is draggable, and no longer uses the old shallow template outputs
Run API/web typechecks, targeted action generation tests, targeted Home tests, and browser verification of the Top of Mind action post-it on desktop and mobile
userStories.notes: Product correction: the current action checklist is a placeholder UI built from actionForThoughtCard(card), so the actions can feel weird and generic. This must become a real ambition-learning loop: actions are not productivity tasks, they are small real-world experiments that create new personal context. They should feel like the next thing a reflective person would actually try after noticing a pattern in their saved inspirations.

userStories.title: Build true action recommender learning loop
userStories.description: As a user, I want WAKA's action post-it to recommend personally grounded real-world experiments from my evolving personal context, not frontend templates dressed up as recommendations.
acceptanceCriteria: Move action recommendation out of Home.tsx template helpers into a dedicated recommender layer that can run from backend/API or shared domain code and be tested independently

Model each recommended action as structured data with id, text, sourceTopOfMindId, sourceSignalIds, evidence snippets, action kind, whyNow rationale, confidence, createdAt, status, and dismissed/completed timestamps where appropriate

Generate recommendations from current Top of Mind notes plus supporting saved inspirations, highlights, user-written resonance notes, repeated motifs, recently reactivated memories, and rejected/anti-environment signals
Rank actions by personal-context usefulness: actions should help the user learn about people, place, work, taste, identity, rejection, or next experiment rather than optimize productivity

Require every recommendation to name a concrete 24-72 hour real-world move such as message a specific kind of person, enter a specific type of room, make and show a rough artifact, remove an environmental pull, test a career/build hunch, or revisit a saved inspiration with a concrete external action
Reject actions that are generic, self-help flavored, template-shaped, broad life advice, reflective homework, corporate productivity language, or merely a paraphrase of the Top of Mind post-it

Use completion/removal feedback as learning signals: completed actions should strengthen the source pattern only after a follow-up captured signal or explicit user note; removed actions should reduce similar future suggestions
Persist action state locally or through the API so done/removed actions do not reappear after refresh and can be used by the recommender on the next run
Show only the top five active high-confidence recommendations on the draggable action post-it; hide low-confidence slots entirely
Keep the action post-it draggable with the same paper interaction affordance as Top of Mind notes
Add unit tests for the recommender ranking/filtering that fail on generic template outputs and disconnected evidence
Add API or integration tests proving completed/removed actions affect future recommendations
Add Home tests proving persisted active actions render, completed/removed actions disappear after refresh, and the action post-it remains draggable
Run API/web typechecks, recommender tests, Home tests, and browser verification on localhost desktop and mobile
userStories.notes: Product correction after US-036: the current implementation still generates actions in the frontend from deterministic phrase templates. The target is a real self-improving personal-context action loop. Actions are not a to-do list. They are small experiments that create new evidence about the user's ambition and feed back into future Top of Mind and action recommendations.
